text: What works: the ridgelines recede in layers of haze, giving real depth, and the hill's edge dropping past the quarry scar to the sea makes a strong diagonal against the flat coastline. Bright overcast light is soft and even, like a giant softbox, so the greens keep their detail. Change one thing: the bottom half is empty grass with no line to follow. Crouch low and use the worn path or the rocks at bottom right as a lead-in from a corner towards the quarry, with the horizon on the upper third, so the land does the pointing. Relates to: the establishing extreme wide, the opener that tells a music video where we are; the light is diffused soft top light. Exercise: find one real line tomorrow (kerb, rail, path) and shoot it three ways in five minutes: entering from the bottom-left corner, dead centre, and with the horizon high. Note which pulls your eye furthest in.
